text.en: Bratu fold continuation and Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov The same one-dimensional Bratu problem compares fold continuation and matrix-free iteration against an independently evaluated analytic family. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-bratu-continuation-jfnk-2026-11-24-r2 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Crossing the Bratu fold with pseudo-arclength continuation Follow the lower and upper branches of the same one-dimensional Bratu boundary-value problem; check tangents, the fold and spatial error against an independent analytic family. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless x in [0,1] with zero Dirichlet endpoints and 31/63/127 interior nodes. Take 80 fixed ds=0.1 steps from the zero solution. Correct both branches at lambda=2; lambda=4 is a deliberate discrete no-solution control. Pseudo-arclength is not physical time. Editorial clarification A small one-dimensional simple fold only. The whole-curve family comparison uses the computed midpoint as its family coordinate and is distinct from the independent fixed-lambda profile checks. The continuum fold is not an exact discrete solution. No general bifurcation-tracking or large-scale performance claim. Adopted numerical method Use a unit tangent in h-sum(du squared)+d-lambda squared, a predictor and a tangent-hyperplane Newton corrector. A separate augmented system locates the fold and a normalized null vector. This case deliberately assembles sparse Jacobians. −u′′=λeu,u(0)=u(1)=0 uθ=2log⁡cosh⁡(θ/2)cosh⁡(θ(x−1/2)),λ(θ)=2θ2/cosh⁡2(θ/2) References and measured quantities The preserved R3 run passed the shared 27 pytest tests and this case’s 67 fixed gates. Discrete residuals, tangent orientation/normalization, fold/null/transversality conditions, an independent Decimal80 family and fixed three-grid errors are checked separately. Verification limits and failures A small one-dimensional simple fold only. The whole-curve family comparison uses the computed midpoint as its family coordinate and is distinct from the independent fixed-lambda profile checks. The continuum fold is not an exact discrete solution. No general bifurcation-tracking or large-scale performance claim. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded. Acceptance uses original fixed-input tolerances and unrounded numbers; only stored results passing every check are presented. 量 / metricMeasured value fold_orders[2.0003257002223824,2.000081417263765] Jacobian-free Newton–Krylov with analytic, central-FD and directional-AD products Solve both Bratu branches with three Jv choices without assembling the nonlinear Jacobian; retain forcing, actual residuals and evaluation counts. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries The same dimensionless one-dimensional Dirichlet problem at lambda=3, 63/127 interior nodes, starting from zero or 4sin(pi*x).
